programs.title: Attenborough's Wonder of Song
programs.desc: Sir David Attenborough selects seven of the most extraordinary recordings from the natural world and explores what these sounds mean to specific animal species.Each song - from that of a lemur, through the song of a humpback whale or a lyrebird from the order of passerine birds - was recorded during the lifetime of a famous naturalist who recorded and analyzed these songs for decades.The oldest recording was made when Sir David was five years old, the latest just a few years before the documentary was created.Each has an amazing story behind it and shows how much we still don't know about the natural world.When Sir David Attenborough was born, the science of song was transformed under Charles Darwin's theory of sexual selection, which labeled singing dangerous because it revealed the singer's location to predators.The same singing also gives males a great chance to be noticed by the female, and thus to pass on their genes to the next bird generation.So the males sing, and the females listen and choose the best singers because, according to them, they will be the best fathers.New scientific trends in bird song are challenging these long-held ideas.Scientists invited to the program show that in fact, in most species of songbirds, females create their own songs - and only now do they have a chance to be truly heard.However, there is a concern as to whether we will be able to learn all the songs of these extraordinary birds - the human loss is loud and the planet Earth is falling silently, as the host of the program also warns.The production is a continuation of the Grierson Award-nominated documentary "The Egg: A Miracle of Nature".

programs.title: Attenborough's Birds of Paradise
programs.desc: David Attenborough presents his own perspective on the scientific discoveries, facts and myths surrounding the birds of paradise.He spent half his life filming and researching their habits both in the depths of the forest and in museums and nature collections in Europe.It tells the story of the fascination these birds arouse in the hearts of various people.Viewers will also learn what science says about them and their unusual behavior.In the final part of the program, David will take viewers to Qatar, where the world's largest breeding of birds of paradise has been established in a state-of-the-art facility.

programs.title: Attenborough and the Jurassic Sea Monster
programs.desc: Sir David Attenborough accompanies a team of scientists to observe a skeleton found in Dorset.Together they examine the skull of a huge pliosaur.The reptile was named the marine tyrannosaurus.

programs.title: Mammals - Making Of
programs.desc: Behind the scenes of the production of a nature production presenting the life of mammals.The most diverse phylum of the animal kingdom includes both the tiny Etruscan shrew and the blue whale.

programs.title: Life Below Zero: The Thaw
programs.desc: Alaskans are preparing for a thaw.Snow-covered peaks turn into obstacle courses.Hikers encounter rushing streams and hungry predators and swarms of insects.

programs.title: Exploration Volcano
programs.desc: Chris Horsley specializes in volcano exploration.In the program, he brings documentarians from around the world to volcanic trails to show them the effects of eruptions, which can wreak havoc and threaten communities.Chris's great expedition spans a wide range - from the jungles of the Congo to the lava-burnt cities of the Canary Islands, from the distinctive glacial plains of Iceland to the smoking archipelagos of Italy.In each episode, his team must face unique and unpredictable terrain.However, the team does not stop at anything.He wants to complete each mission, whether it's collecting molten lava straight from the source or installing state-of-the-art volcano monitoring systems.These activities are necessary to better understand the functioning of ruthless natural giants.
